title: weekly-skim-briefs-mira-chen-2026-09-21
content:
Goal: quick synthesis of 3 things I read this week and concrete small experiments to run on the sandbox cluster. Keep it actionable and snackable — for my own memory and to hand off to Owen/Talia for pair time.

Top-level takeaway (one line): small, asymmetric evictions + rough LRU quantization awareness can significantly reduce cold-kv overheads for multi-session chat workloads without obvious quality regressions when combined with a short-term prefix cache. Worth a focused micro-experiment next sprint.

Papers / posts skimmed (very condensed):

1) "Adaptive KV Eviction for Long-Context Decoders" (arXiv preprint, 2026) — quick notes:
- Proposition: not full LRU — instead maintain two-tier ages: 'active' window (last N tokens per session) + session-level score (importance heuristics). Evict from background sessions first, degrade longest sessions minimally.
- Methods: simulated chat workloads, token-level perplexity + synthetic QA accuracy. They show 15–25% reduction in memory footprint for same latency SLOs.
- Key caveat: their "importance heuristics" rely on response-salience signals (click/feedback) that we don't have in sandbox. But our routing + token-level latencies could be a proxy.
- Why I care: matches a common Redwood Hosted pain: many long idle sessions holding large KV caches. If we can reclaim memory early and re-synth with prefix caching we get better packing for Dedicated pools.

2) "Prefix Cache Strategies for Prefix-sensitive LLMs" (conference talk notes) — quick notes:
- Idea: keep short (<=128 token) prefix embeddings/KV snapshots for frequently used system prompts or initial user context. On cold session restore, load prefix snapshot before streaming remainder of KV.
- Measured effect: 30–60ms median reduction at 512 seq-length for models with heavy positional recalc cost.
- Implementation notes: snapshot size matters (tradeoff persistent memory vs reconstruction cost), and snapshot invalidation is tricky for dynamic system prompts.
- Why I care: Redwood Optimize suggestions could recommend prefix-snapshotting for customers using chat templates. Also reduces token spend on re-priming.

3) "Quantization-aware Eviction and Rehydration" (blog + notebook) — quick notes:
- Practical trick: quantized KV shards (e.g., 4-bit) are much cheaper in memory but slower to rehydrate; authors recommend demoting cold shards to quantized storage and rehydrate to full-precision in background when load predicts re-use.
- Found ~40% memory saving vs naive keep-all full-precision, with rehydration CPU/GPU overhead manageable if staggered.
- Takeaway: for Dedicated and Private installs this fits well — we could add a storage tier (hot full-precision, warm quantized, cold compressed on SSD) controlled by our Autoscaler policies.

Immediate micro-experiments (sandbox, 1–2 dev-days each):

A) Two-tier eviction + prefix snapshot baseline
- What: implement a simple heuristic: keep 'active window' = last 128 tokens per session pinned; compute session score = max(last_activity_ts, recent_response_length*0.1). Evict oldest low-score sessions first. Integrate with prefix snapshot loader that stores 128-token snapshot per session id in in-memory map keyed by model+system-prompt-hash.
- Metrics to collect: % reclaimed KV memory, cold-start latency 95th percentile, QA accuracy on synthetic retrieval prompts (to detect degradation).
- Acceptance: >=12% reclaimed memory with <5% accuracy drop and <20ms increase 95p latency.
- Owners: me (proto), Owen (runtime integration). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 (placeholder linked).

B) Quantized demotion pipeline (prototype)
- What: pipeline that serializes evicted shards to quantized format (4-bit) on NVMe, marks metadata in session store. On predicted re-use, rehydrate to GPU async.
- Quick smoke: run on a controlled set of 100 synthetic conversations with heavy idle tails and measure rehydrate cost + failed predictions.
- Danger: if rehydration pressure spikes we could overload device; include simple rate limiter.
- Owner: Talia (serialize helpers), me (predictor heuristics).

C) Prefix snapshot cache TTL experiments
- What: try different prefix snapshot TTLs (30s, 2m, 10m) for a steady stream of templated chat sessions. Measure hit rate, median latency improvement, and memory cost.
- Quick thought: start with 2m TTL as default — balances typical desktop chat session behavior.

Notes-to-self: risk flags and open questions
- How does prefix snapshot interact with model compilation/kernels? If snapshot uses different kv-layout (e.g., fused attention kernels), snapshot restore must be compiled for runtime or we pay heavy recompilation costs. Need to talk to infra (Kenji?) about snapshot ABI.
- On Private installs, storage tiers must respect KMS/HSM rules — quantized storage still sensitive; get security sign-off before recommending to customers.
- Need to instrument token-level origin metadata (why a token was generated) to later attribute quality regressions to eviction policy vs model quantization. Add a "rehydration-cause" tag in logs.

Quick links to follow-ups / context:
- JIRA: RI-2143 (KV eviction heuristic spike); add subtask for "prefix-snapshot experiment"
- Slack: ping #serving-runtime and @kenji for kernel ABI constraints
- Related Confluence doc: KV Eviction notes (linked above) has older heuristics from 2025 — compare metric definitions.

Action items (next 7 days):
- Today: sketch proto in runtime sandbox (me) — 2–3 hours.
- Tomorrow: sync 30m with Owen to scope PR and integration plan.
- Wed: Talia to prototype quantized serialization helper (half-day).
- Fri: run small synthetic workload (1000 sessions) and collect baseline metrics.
- Next Monday: decide go/no-go for adding heuristic to canary cluster.

Random musings / heuristics to remember:
- Prefer conservative thresholds early (evict only when reclaiming > 8% mem) to avoid oscillation.
- Give session scoring a short cooldown to avoid ping-pong where sessions keep being evicted and rehydrated.
- Quick rule-of-thumb: if prefix-hit rate > 20% then snapshotting likely pays off for chat templates.

Questions for group sync:
- Kenji: kernel / compiled-ABI compatibility for fast KV snapshot restore?
- SRE: if we offload many evicted shards to NVMe, what are SLO implications for IO bursts?
- Product: should Redwood Console's Optimize tab expose a "suggest snapshot" toggle per customer?

Closing note: want to keep this short. If experiments look promising, write a short doc for Product proposing "Prefix snapshot + quantized demotion" as a Redwood Optimize feature (small UI knob + runtime policy). If not, we at least get clearer instrumentation and some useful heuristics.

-- mira
